The test image shows soybean plants with mostly green foliage but noticeable yellowing/chlorosis on some leaves, particularly in the lower canopy. Some leaves appear tan/dead among the green. No obvious spots, pustules, or powdery coating visible. The yellowing pattern with lower leaf death while upper leaves remain green is a key diagnostic feature.

Top candidates: Sudden_death_syndrome (interveinal chlorosis, lower leaf death), Brown_Stem_Rot (similar foliar symptoms), Phytophthora (yellowing + stem rot).

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The SDS reference shows very distinct interveinal chlorosis with green veins and brown/yellow necrotic tissue between them — a dramatic pattern. The test image, being a whole-plant field view, shows scattered yellowing of lower/inner leaves while upper canopy stays green, with some dead tan leaves mixed in. The specific interveinal pattern isn't visible at this scale, but the overall plant-level presentation (lower leaf death, upper canopy intact) is consistent with SDS at mid-season.

The SDS reference confirms the disease progresses to dramatic leaf necrosis — what we see in the test image matches early-to-mid stage SDS presentation at the whole-plant level.

{"prediction": "Sudden_death_syndrome", "confidence": 0.45, "reasoning": "Whole-plant view shows scattered yellowing and death of lower/inner leaves while upper canopy remains largely green — consistent with mid-season SDS presentation. The close-up interveinal chlorosis pattern diagnostic of SDS isn't visible at this scale, but the overall progression pattern (lower leaf yellowing/death, intact upper canopy, some tan dead leaf tissue) fits SDS better than alternatives like Brown Stem Rot or Phytophthora at this whole-plant view."}
